decisions.rationale: The source id column has distinct_count 10760 equal to row_count 10760 with null_rate 0.0, so runway_id (the cast of id) uniquely identifies a runway record and is declared as the grain.
The profile reports duplicate_row_rate 0.0 across row_count 10760, so no exact duplicate rows exist in bronze and no dedupe step is needed.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta carry is_airbyte_metadata: true and describe the ingestion run, not runways, so all three are dropped.
lighted and closed landed as DECIMAL(38,9) with distinct_values exactly [0.0, 1.0] and null_rate 0.0; they are cast to BOOLEAN and renamed is_lighted and is_closed.
id and airport_ref landed as VARCHAR but every sample is a pure integral digit string; both are cast to INTEGER to support numeric joins to the airports table.

le_displaced_threshold_ft and he_displaced_threshold_ft have null_rates 0.884201 and 0.899907 respectively; absence means no displaced threshold is recorded, so both are kept nullable with nulls retained rather than imputed or dropped.

surface has 239 distinct values with many spellings of the same material ('ASP', 'ASPH', 'ASP/CONC', 'ASPH-CONC-G'); normalization is a semantic mapping deferred to a later layer, so the raw value is kept.

length_ft includes min 0.0 and he_heading_degt includes max 362.0, which exceed plausible physical bounds; these values are retained as landed and flagged here for reviewer awareness rather than silently corrected.

purpose: silver_ourairports_runways is the cleaned, typed runway reference table derived from bronze ourairports_runways: one row per runway (grain runway_id) with typed dimensions, boolean lighting/closure flags, and low-end (le_) and high-end (he_) endpoint coordinates, elevations, headings, and displaced thresholds. It feeds airport-level analytics by joining to the airports table on airport_ref or airport_ident.
usage: Join to the airports table on airport_ref (numeric) or airport_ident (code). Filter on is_closed = false to analyze active runways. Endpoint columns (le_/he_ latitude, longitude, elevation, heading) are null for roughly 22-28% of rows and displaced thresholds for roughly 88-90%, so consumers must handle nulls explicitly; surface is raw uncleaned text and should be normalized by the consumer before grouping.
limitations: Nulls are retained rather than imputed: le/he coordinates and headings are missing at rates of 0.221-0.276, displaced thresholds at 0.884 and 0.900. The surface column's 239 distinct raw spellings are not normalized. Out-of-range values landed in the source are kept as-is, including length_ft of 0.0 and he_heading_degt up to 362.0, and le_ident/he_ident contain junk values like '.' and '-'. No duplicate removal was applied because duplicate_row_rate is 0.0.
